messages.author: 3132b1ef78b4baf1
messages.subject: Factors in Hurdle Model
parts:
Hi INLA group,

I am attempting to fit a Hurdle Poisson model in INLA and have run into an issue with the factors defined. I have been following the Likelihood for hurdle model thread to define a model using the bioChemist data from the pscl package. I have attached reproducible code to help explain the problem but the issue seems to be with the term 'z.fem' in the model. 

z.fem should be a factor of Men and Women with the reference being 'Men'. So when I fit the model, I am expecting to see only 'z.femWomen' in the fixed effects. However I am seeing both 'z.femMen' and 'z.femWomen'. These two fixed effects , along with the 'z.intercept' term, have extremely large credible intervals as well which made me realised there could be an issue. However, I have no idea how to fix the issue. As part of the Hurdle model, I defined the same fixed effects for the count part of the model (prefixed with 'y.'). For 'y.fem' there is not the same issue.

If anyone was able to offer some advice that would be great!

Thanks !!
Connor

messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Re: Factors in Hurdle Model
parts:
Those effects seem to be confounded.

I tried to model fem and mar as random effects, and add constrains, which solved the problem.
...
 f(z.fem, model = "iid", constr=T) +
 f(z.mar, model = "iid", constr=T) + 
...
f(y.fem, model = "iid", constr=T) +
f(y.mar, model = "iid", constr=T) + 
...

parts:
you can do that manully, doing this change

##z.intercept + z.fem + z.mar + z.kid5 + z.phd + z.ment +
z.fem + z.mar + z.kid5 + z.phd + z.ment +
